regimens.indication: Improvement of Neurological Outcome by Reducing Ischemic Deficits in Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (aSAH)

refs.quote: NYMALIZE is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker indicated for the improvement of neurological outcome by reducing the incidence and severity of ischemic deficits in adult patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) from ruptured intracranial berry aneurysms regardless of their post-ictus neurological condition (i.e., Hunt and Hess Grades I-V). ( 1 )

Administer only enterally (e.g., oral, nasogastric tube, or gastric tube route). Do not administer intravenously or by other parenteral routes. ( 2.1 ) Give one hour before a meal or two hours after a meal. ( 2.1 ) Start dosing within 96 hours of the SAH. ( 2.1 ) Recommended dose is 10 mL (60 mg) every 4 hours for 21 consecutive days. ( 2.2 )

regimens.dose_text: 60 mg (10 mL oral solution) enterally every 4 hours for 21 consecutive days. Initiate within 96 hours of SAH onset. Give 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. WARNING: Administer ONLY enterally (oral, NG, or PEG tube). NEVER administer intravenously (fatal cardiovascular collapse has occurred with IV administration of nimodipine).

regimens.indication: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage in Patients with Cirrhosis (Dose-Reduced)

refs.quote: Patients with Cirrhosis: Reduce dosage to 5 mL (30 mg) every 4 hours. ( 2.4 )

regimens.dose_text: Reduce dosage to 30 mg (5 mL) enterally every 4 hours for 21 consecutive days in patients with cirrhosis.

value.instructions: Administer only enterally (oral, nasogastric tube, or gastric tube route). For NG/gastric tube: administer 10 mL (60 mg) every 4 hours with supplied oral syringe, then refill syringe with 10 mL of 0.9% saline solution and flush tube into stomach. NEVER administer intravenously.

refs.quote: Nasogastric or Gastric Tube Administration: Administer 10 mL (60 mg) every 4 hours with supplied prefilled oral syringe. Refill syringe with 10 mL of 0.9% saline water solution; flush remaining contents from nasogastric or gastric tube into stomach. ( 2.3 )

mechanism_of_action.value: Nimodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. The contractile processes of smooth muscle cells are dependent upon calcium ions, which enter these cells during depolarization as slow ionic transmembrane currents. Nimodipine inhibits calcium ion transfer into these cells and thus inhibits contractions of vascular smooth muscle.
